title: Imbalanced Data
motto: When 99% of your data is "normal," accuracy is a lie.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: When 99% of your data is "normal," accuracy is a lie.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: You build a fraud detection model. It gets 99.9% accuracy. You celebrate. Then you realize it predicts "not fraud" for every single transaction.

This is not a bug. It is the rational thing to do when only 0.1% of transactions are fraudulent. The model learns that always guessing the majority class minimizes overall error. It is technically correct and completely useless.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: Rare classes need oversampling or class weights. Accuracy lies when 99% of emails are not spam.

steps.title: Implement imbalance
steps.body: Write the function from scratch in the workspace. Run when ready — all tests must pass.
